rows.adsb_note: CORROBORATED IN THE AIR, NOT ON THE GROUND. Closest recovered position is 1.7 km from KILG at -105 ft above the field - an arrival, a departure or a low pass. The only on-ground positions in this trace are at KPVU (Provo Municipal Airport). It places NOBODY aboard.
rows.source: Compilation spreadsheet circulated by trackers; alternate tracker read @troofevades (takeoff ~13:14 UTC, landing ~16:52 UTC); audit index 41 (flight confirmed, origin corrected from 'Paris' to Provo)
rows.counterargument: 'NEBRASKA/DELAWARE' IS NOT A LOCATION - it is two states 1,200 miles apart offered as alternatives in a cell that should hold one place. NO AIRCRAFT IN THIS FLEET WAS IN NEBRASKA ON 10 SEP 2025: the Lincoln rotation ran 17-23 August and did not resume until 5-11 October, so half the claimed location has no aircraft behind it at all. The Delaware half has an aircraft, but Wilmington is the aircraft's ordinary destination - it appears on the OUTBOUND leg of twenty-one rotations across three years, and ONLY ever the outbound leg. Erika Kirk has said she stayed home in Arizona with her mother that day. Neither version is independently documented.
rows.notes: ADDED FROM THE OVERLAP PAGE, which had no row in this file. ERIKA'S SIDE IS THE WEAK SIDE and this row is the concrete form of it: the flight is audited and confirmed, the Kirk-side location is an unverified spreadsheet cell that the person it describes has contradicted. Her flight logs are reported erased - see site/docs/Planes/Erika-Flight-Logs-Erased.mdx. Erika Kirk is a living person, not charged with anything, named here only as the subject of a disputed claim she has denied.

flights.source: PRIMARY ADS-B POSITION DATA pulled by this repo 24 Aug 2026 from the free ADS-B Exchange monthly globe sample (samples.adsbexchange.com/traces) - source row ADSB-004. The trace self-identifies its own registration and type. Positions resolved to the nearest named field with the CC0 OurAirports gazetteer (ADSB-005).
flights.notes: CLAIM: none - this leg was not previously claimed by any tracker; it is a leg THIS REPO SOURCED ITSELF from primary data, and it is the EARLIEST US position we hold for this aircraft. ON THE GROUND at Wilmington DE (KILG), first fix 11:31:13 UTC at 0.71 km, still on the ground 11:32:38 UTC at 0.68 km - 9 on-ground points. It then departs and the day ends at 22:31:43 UTC descending through 500 ft over ALMAZA AIR FORCE BASE, Cairo (HEAZ, 1.38 km) - an Egyptian MILITARY field, not Cairo International. 1,508 trace points. This is one of the three sampled 2022 days that put SU-BTT in the United States, and it is primary corroboration for the DELAWARE leg of the site's previously unverified Missouri/Delaware/Utah/Nebraska/Kansas clustering claim. SAMPLING CAVEAT - PUBLISH THIS EVERY TIME THIS ROW IS CITED: the ADS-B Exchange free sample holds ONE DAY PER MONTH, THE 1ST, AND NOTHING ELSE. This row establishes that the aircraft WAS here on this date. It says NOTHING about how often it came, and it is not a stay of known length - the end_date is the same sampled day because that is the only day the archive holds. COUNTERARGUMENT: a single sampled day at a field with routine transatlantic customs and bizjet maintenance traffic is not by itself evidence of anything, and no Kirk or TPUSA presence is documented at this field on this date.
